thread.title_full: Chronically Ill People on Medicaid Won't Be Bound by New Work Requirement Rules

author: Fatima Hussein Associated Press
title: Chronically Ill People on Medicaid Won't Be Bound by New Work Requirement Rules
text:
• A federal judge ruled that chronically ill people on Medicaid won't be bound by new work requirement rules.
• The rules were part of the latest Trump administration guidance to qualify for "medically frail" exemptions.
• The judge's decision affects people who are on Medicaid and have chronic illnesses.
• The Trump administration's guidance was aimed at requiring people on Medicaid to work or participate in work-related activities to qualify for benefits.
• The judge's ruling blocks the Trump administration's plan to implement the work requirement rules.
• The decision was made in response to a lawsuit filed by a group of states and advocacy groups.
• The judge found that the Trump administration's guidance was unlawful and did not follow proper procedures.
• The ruling does not affect other Medicaid work requirements that have been implemented in some states.
• The decision is a victory for advocates who argued that the work requirements would harm vulnerable populations.
• The Trump administration has not commented on the ruling.
• The judge's decision is likely to be appealed by the Trump administration.
